direction: Use budget-adaptive construction (regret-2 / nearest-neighbor-guided insertion with k-nearest candidate seeding) followed by first-improvement 2-opt over truncated neighbor lists (k≈16-20), restarting construction from a different seed while time budget remains, so 500 ms is spent on repeated cheap improvement rather than one expensive full pass.

operations.mechanism: The active template is tsp_guided_insertion_2opt with postprocess 'none'; only the interior hook (score_insertion_move and neighbor evaluation) is tunable this round. Diagnostic hook evaluation failed on tool-side signature/code errors rather than solver evidence, so the first round should establish a clean, self-contained hook that (1) is non-empty valid UTF-8 source, (2) exploits candidate lists to make 2-opt moves O(1)-ish in practice, and (3) uses elapsed-time checks for safe restarts — the standard mechanism for converting extra budget into tour-length gains on TSP. This also produces the reference signature needed to populate the currently empty archive frontier and gives a measurable baseline for later neighbour-list size and regret-k ablations.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Under a 500 ms per-instance budget on tsp_guided_insertion_2opt, replacing a single greedy cheapest-insertion + full-matrix 2-opt sweep with (a) regret-2 guided insertion over a k-nearest-neighbor candidate set and (b) first-improvement 2-opt restricted to those candidate lists, plus seed restarts, yields a shorter final tour length than the plain insertion/2-opt baseline while staying inside the deterministic time budget, because candidate-list restriction cuts per-move cost so many more improving moves are evaluated per millisecond.
